title: Last Bell, 2012
logline: The bell at 3:05 PM. Wood is asleep; he works nights. It wakes him through the garage wall. He draws it lying down, badly, on purpose.

panels.composition: The garage, daylight through the sill, blinds down. WOOD asleep on the cot. BARNABY on the floor. The bell, faint, from across town.

image.prompt: a garage studio in daylight with the blinds down, a man asleep on a cot and an old dog on the floor, a faint distant bell sound, razor-sharp ink

panels.composition: Wood's eye open. The bell. Thirteen years of hearing it from wherever he was.

image.prompt: close-up of a man's one eye open on a pillow, listening

panels.composition: Wood drawing on the pad lying down, the pad held over his face. The line, from that angle, is bad. Deliberately bad. The strip's first bad line since 1997 and it's a joke.

image.prompt: a man lying on a cot drawing on a pad held above his face, the drawing crude and shaky
image.notes: Panel 3's inset drawing is scratchy, crow-quill-bad — Era I's line for one panel. The rest of the strip pristine.

panels.composition: The drawing: the school, the steps, the kids, the bell shape — all in the 1997 line. Under it, in the 2012 hand: 3:05. Still.

image.prompt: close-up of a drawing pad showing a school at the last bell drawn in a scratchy crude zine style, with a small precise note beneath it

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: The bell wakes him. He draws it in the old line, lying down. '3:05. Still.'
